_README: Labelled retrieval set for scope Section 10 'retrieval precision (RAG)'
and Section 2.1.4, which asks for precision@k as a first-class number.
HOW THE LABELS WERE MADE. Each `answer_contains` phrase was located in the
source PDF by string search, and `gold_pages` records every page it was
found on. The labels therefore come from the document, not from the
system's output and not from memory.
HOW THE QUESTIONS WERE WRITTEN. Deliberately NOT in the document's own
wording. 'How much do I have to deposit to bid?' rather than 'What is the
Earnest Money Deposit of Rs. 31,500?'. A question that quotes its own
answer measures string matching and flatters a dense retriever that may be
SCORING. A retrieved chunk counts as relevant when it contains the phrase
(whitespace- and case-normalised). This is strict in a useful direction: a
chunk that is topically about EMD but omits the figure does not count, so
the metric tracks 'could a vendor read the answer off this chunk' rather

LABEL CORRECTIONS. q11 and q16 were fixed after a first measurement run: q16's phrase list held only one of two wordings the tender uses for the same fact, and q11's question did not describe the clause it was labelled against. Both were harness defects that understated retrieval. Entries carry a _label_fix note. No label was broadened merely because the system missed it -- q06, q12, q13, q14 and q17 remain scored as misses.
